summary: R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) was an Indologist who earned a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.
R. T. Vyas is an Indologist who served as General Editor of Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1988) and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1993–1994).

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University (~1942–1946). He held positions at Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras, and Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).

R. Venkatraman is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, later serving there as Reader (attested 1990).

Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at St. Xavier's Collegiate School (~1875–1876) and University College London (~1878–1880), and founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.

Rachael Margaret Griffiths works in Tibetology and computational studies. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford (-2020) and held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2023) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (2024).
Philosopher Rachael Wiseman studied at the University of York and became a Reader at the University of Liverpool in 2023.

Rachel H. Pang works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia and was appointed Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College (attested 2019).

Rachel Van Meter Baumer (1928–1995) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1958–1964) and under Thomas Welbourne Clark (~1961–1963). She taught at Michigan State University and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1969–1977).

Rachelle M. Scott works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and served as Associate Professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (post 2002; attested 2009–2017).

Rade Uhlik (1899–1991) was a linguist and Indologist who studied Germanistics at the University of Belgrade (~1920–1925). He worked as a translator for Tanjug (~1945–1947) and as a custos at the National Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina (~1947–1964).

Radha Burnier (1923–2013) worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Kalakshetra and Banaras Hindu University (~1945–1950) and served as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1960–1980).

Radha Krishna Choudhary (1921–1985) was a historian and Indologist who studied at Tej Narayan Banaili College and Patna University. He headed the History Department at Ganesh Dutt College (1946) and taught at Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University (1974–1984).

Radha Kumud Mukherjee (1884–1963) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1901–1905). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1916–1917) and Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1917–1921).

Radhey Kishori works in computational fields and Indology. She held faculty posts at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University, Agra (2012–2014) and Dr. MPS Group of Institutions, later becoming Assistant Professor at the Institute of Innovation in Technology and Management (2022–2024).

Radhika Herzberger (born 1938) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto (~1976–1982) under Bimal Krishna Matilal and served as Director of Rishi Valley School (~1980–2012).

Radoslav Katičić (1930–2019) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Zagreb (~1949–1954) and under Paul Thieme (~1956–1958). He held a post at the University of Vienna (~1977–1998) and was a member of the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts.

Rafal Stepien works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure (attested 2015), and held posts at Wadham College (2012–2013) and Harvard University (attested 2015).
Rafał Felbur is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who was a PhD candidate at Stanford University (attested 2015). He studied under Paul Harrison, John R. McRae, and Luis Oscar Gómez.
Raffaele Catà is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed a laurea at the University of Bologna (2011–2012) under the supervision of Manlio Iofrida and Saverio Marchignoli.
